westminster.name: Westminster
westminster.description: The political and royal heart of London, Westminster combines world-famous landmarks with elegant residential enclaves. From the grandeur of Belgravia to the village feel of Marylebone, it attracts diplomats, policy professionals, and finance executives who demand centrality and prestige.
westminster.demographic: MPs, policy advisors, diplomats, finance executives, established professionals aged 30–55

camden.name: Camden
camden.description: Camden is London's creative powerhouse — a vibrant mix of alternative culture, tech innovation, and beautiful residential streets. From the iconic Camden Market to the leafy heights of Hampstead and the intellectual buzz of Bloomsbury, it's the borough of choice for creatives, tech founders, and media professionals.
camden.demographic: Creatives, tech entrepreneurs, academics, media professionals, musicians, ages 22–45

kensington-chelsea.name: Kensington & Chelsea
kensington-chelsea.description: The Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea represents the pinnacle of prime central London living. White stucco terraces, garden squares, and world-class museums define this affluent enclave. Home to international diplomats, private equity partners, and established families seeking exceptional schools and discreet luxury.
kensington-chelsea.demographic: High-net-worth international families, diplomats, private equity, entrepreneurs, ages 35–60

tower-hamlets.name: Tower Hamlets
tower-hamlets.description: Tower Hamlets is London's fastest-transforming borough, anchored by the Canary Wharf financial district and stretching to vibrant East End neighbourhoods. From slick riverside towers to converted warehouses in Shoreditch and Bethnal Green, it offers a compelling mix of urban energy, green space, and relative value.
tower-hamlets.demographic: Finance professionals, tech workers, young families, university staff, ages 24–40
